subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class cron output targets, and what security and product rules should govern file writes, channel fan-out, session injection, silent discard, fallback, and run-status reporting?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix creates new framework-owned file, channel, and cross-session delivery authority that automation should not define without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design One Output Contract
options.body: Define a single cron output target API with explicit authorization, path policy, delivery semantics, docs, protocol support, and regression tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Delivery Defaults
options.body: Defer file and session targets and solve only the focused default-recipient problem tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/9155.

options.title: Reject Core Output Targets
options.body: Keep cron routing prompt/tool-driven or plugin-owned and improve diagnostics/docs instead of adding new core delivery authority.

recommendation.title: Design One Output Contract
recommendation.body: Define a single cron output target API with explicit authorization, path policy, delivery semantics, docs, protocol support, and regression tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent code and issue-history signal for cron delivery policy and is already connected to this discussion.
